headline: Going Commando's USA v1.01 jumps from 15.46% to 44.26% matched code
summary: Two large batches take Going Commando's USA v1.01 progress report to 44.26% matched code and 5,514 of 8,584 functions, up from 15.46%. A matched function compiles to exactly the same bytes as the original game. #333 adds 777 USA v1.01 functions and three release-specific ones, including large hero-state handlers, alongside compiler and assembler fixes measured against the original. #334 follows with 119 smaller functions, including four whose starting points were corrected to exclude linker filler.
highlights: The large source totals are dominated by #333, whose biggest hero-state handlers span tens of thousands of bytes. Its work was reconciled with implementations already merged from other contributors.
Particle routines (#335), functions reused from Ratchet & Clank (#336), and further small-function batches (#337, #339, #340, #343) opened but had not merged.
#338 proposes classifying six hardware wait loops as handwritten assembly. #342 proposes a separate home for functional, non-matching C that would receive no matching credit.
One level function remains assembly in Europe/Australia and USA v2.00, with explicit assembly units added for those releases.
